content.value_statement: Agent changes can improve one quality dimension while weakening another. This skill provides rubrics, test-set design, scoring methods, and monitoring patterns for measurable evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Defines weighted dimensions for factual accuracy, completeness, citation accuracy, source quality, and tool efficiency.
Guides test-set design across simple, medium, complex, and extended agent tasks.
Provides Python utilities for rubric scoring, test filtering, result summaries, and pass-rate calculations.
Explains LLM-based, human, end-state, degradation, and continuous evaluation methods.
Tracks sampled production scores, pass rates, quality status, and threshold-based alerts.
limitations: The included evaluator uses demonstration heuristics instead of an LLM judge or human review.
The runner generates simulated outputs and requires integration with a real agent.
Metrics and samples are stored in memory without persistence or dashboard integration.
Production previews are not redacted, so integrations must protect sensitive interaction data.

use_cases.title: Validate an Agent Feature
use_cases.description: Create a weighted rubric and representative tests before comparing a new agent feature against its baseline.

use_cases.title: Establish Release Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Define pass thresholds, edge cases, and regression checks for agent releases across multiple quality dimensions.

use_cases.title: Monitor Production Quality
use_cases.description: Plan sampled evaluations, trend metrics, alerts, and human review for a deployed agent system.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Rubric
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation rubric for [agent task]. Include three quality dimensions, scoring levels, weights, and a clear passing threshold.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start evaluating a new agent workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Representative Test Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test set for [agent workflow]. Cover four complexity levels, common requests, known failures, edge cases, and expected outcomes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expand evaluation beyond a small group of examples.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Agent Configurations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [configuration A] and [configuration B] on the same test set. Define quality, token, latency, and tool-efficiency metrics with decision rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Measure the effect of a model or context change.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Continuous Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design continuous evaluation for [production agent]. Specify sampling, privacy controls, scoring, baselines, alert thresholds, regression gates, trend analysis, and human escalation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Operate an advanced evaluation program in production.

output_examples.input: Create a rubric for a research agent that must cite reliable sources.
output: Factual accuracy: 35 percent, with claims checked against ground truth.
Citation accuracy: 25 percent, with each citation supporting its associated claim.
Source quality: 20 percent, favoring authoritative primary sources.
Completeness: 15 percent, covering every requested topic.
Tool efficiency: 5 percent, avoiding unnecessary searches. Passing score: 75 percent.

output_examples.input: Design tests for a customer support agent.
output: Simple: answer a documented billing question accurately.
Medium: resolve an account issue using two approved tools.
Complex: handle conflicting customer details and request clarification.
Extended: maintain policy compliance across a multi-turn escalation.

output_examples.input: Summarize an evaluation run with 82 passing tests from 100.
output_examples.output: Pass rate: 82 percent. The result misses the 85 percent release threshold. Citation accuracy declined most, so review failed cases before deployment.

best_practices: Evaluate outcomes with multi-dimensional rubrics instead of requiring one execution path.
Use realistic tasks, context sizes, tool access, and complexity distributions.
Track a baseline over time and combine automated scoring with systematic human review.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize for one aggregate score while ignoring dimension-level regressions.
Do not build test sets only from simple or successful interactions.
Do not deploy heuristic scores as authoritative judgments without validation.

faq.question: What types of agents can this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It applies to research, support, analysis, tool-using, and other agents with observable tasks and outputs.

faq.question: Does the skill call an LLM judge automatically?
faq.answer: No. The included Python evaluator uses simple heuristics and describes where LLM or human judgment should be integrated.

faq.question: Can I compare two models or context strategies?
faq.answer: Yes. Run both configurations on the same test set and compare quality, token usage, latency, and tool efficiency.

faq.question: How should I choose a passing threshold?
faq.answer: Set thresholds from business risk, baseline performance, and required quality dimensions. Validate them against reviewed examples.

faq.question: Does the skill support production monitoring?
faq.answer: It provides sampling, pass-rate, status, and alert patterns. Persistence, dashboards, privacy controls, and integrations remain implementation work.

faq.question: Why is human review still needed?
faq.answer: Human reviewers catch subtle factual errors, bias, unusual failures, and rubric weaknesses that automated methods can miss.
